evidence: checks.json: patch_applies=true; no commands were run (no tests, per experiment setup).

Diffing base against generated (excluding .git/venv) shows changes in exactly the five files listed in patch.diff: CHANGELOG.md, docs/source/progress.rst, rich/default_styles.py, rich/progress.py, tests/test_progress.py.
patch.diff contains only added lines plus context; nothing from the original is removed or altered.
generated/rich/progress.py:325-334 places TimeElapsedColumn beside TimeRemainingColumn (base rich/progress.py:325-337), the same module as the other progress columns.
generated/rich/default_styles.py:117 registers "progress.elapsed" in DEFAULT_STYLES, the same dict the reference uses.

generated/rich/progress.py:325 `class TimeElapsedColumn(ProgressColumn)` with no-arg construction and `render(self, task) -> Text` at line 328, matching the reference name, base class, and return type (reference/rich/progress.py:325-331).

The reference also adds a public dataclass field Task.finished_time (reference/rich/progress.py:449); the candidate does not. That omission changes column behavior and is recorded under requirement_intent, not counted here.
The patch adds no import lines; generated/rich/progress.py:333 reuses the existing `timedelta` import that TimeRemainingColumn already uses (base rich/progress.py:336).
The column depends only on public Task.elapsed, so the dependency direction is unchanged.
generated/rich/progress.py:325 subclasses ProgressColumn and implements the abstract render method (base rich/progress.py:189-192 defines it as abstract).
generated/rich/default_styles.py:117 registers the theme style "progress.elapsed", as the reference does (reference.diff, rich/default_styles.py hunk).
The column is not added to the default column tuples (base rich/progress.py:137, 576), which matches the reference; it is only added to the process_renderables demo in the reference.
The patch introduces no new packages and does not touch pyproject.toml or poetry.lock.
timedelta is already imported in the base module (base rich/progress.py:336).
The column lives in rich/progress.py with the other ProgressColumn subclasses and reads only the public Task.elapsed property (base rich/progress.py:467-474).

The reference keeps freeze-at-completion state in Task and Progress (reference/rich/progress.py:449, 832-833, 894-895). The candidate has no such state, so it cannot express the completed-task behavior. That is a requirement_intent gap, not a layering error.
generated/rich/progress.py:325-334 uses the existing ProgressColumn.render extension point, the same pattern as TimeRemainingColumn (base rich/progress.py:325-337).
No parallel rendering path or new hook is introduced.
generated/rich/progress.py:330 reads task.elapsed only; it does not touch private Task internals such as _progress or start_time.
No transport, persistence, or framework concerns are mixed into the column.
Docstring style, the "-:--:--" placeholder, and the progress.<name> style key mirror TimeRemainingColumn (generated/rich/progress.py:325-334 vs base rich/progress.py:325-337).
CHANGELOG.md adds an Added entry under Unreleased (generated CHANGELOG.md:8-12); docs/source/progress.rst gains a column list item (generated docs/source/progress.rst:112).
Test name test_time_elapsed_column mirrors test_time_remaining_column (base tests/test_progress.py:69).

Minor, non-blocking: the new test uses a class-attribute override (generated tests/test_progress.py:353-354) instead of the module's MockClock pattern (base tests/test_progress.py:29-41), and it does not extend test_columns.

Reference freezes elapsed on completion: reference/rich/progress.py:330 `elapsed = task.finished_time if task.finished else task.elapsed`. finished_time is set once completed >= total in update() and advance() (reference/rich/progress.py:832-833 and 894-895).

Candidate always shows live elapsed: generated/rich/progress.py:330 `elapsed = task.elapsed`. grep confirms no finished_time or completion tracking anywhere in generated rich/ or tests/. After a task completes, the candidate keeps counting up, while the reference shows a fixed value.

The reference test pins this. reference/tests/test_progress.py:250-266 adds TimeElapsedColumn to test_columns, and its expected string (reference.diff) shows the completed rows as `0:01:00` (test foo, 12/10) and `0:00:45` (test bar, 16/7) in consecutive frames. MockClock auto-advances on every call (base tests/test_progress.py:36-41) and ProgressColumn.__call__ reads the clock on every render (base rich/progress.py:174), so a live elapsed value would change between those frames. By reading the code, the candidate cannot reproduce those frozen values.

The candidate's own test (generated tests/test_progress.py:350-362) covers only the unstarted case ("-:--:--") and a faked elapsed of 60. It never exercises completion, so it would not catch this gap.

Not counted as failures: the reference-only changes to markup, color, console, palette, and the version bump are unrelated to this feature. The reference's test_columns and test_palette are absent from the candidate, but that is not a deletion. Adding TimeElapsedColumn to the process_renderables demo (reference.diff, process_renderables hunk) is optional and the candidate omits it.
criteria.deficiency: TimeElapsedColumn does not freeze at task completion. It keeps showing live elapsed time after completion, while the reference shows the elapsed time at which the task finished (via Task.finished_time). This requires finished_time tracking in Task and Progress.update/advance, which the candidate does not add, and the reference test_columns expectations for completed rows would not be met.
